analysis.title: Market Intelligence: US Morning Update (2 October 2026)
key_insights: Asia closed mixed on Friday. Hong Kong fell sharply on reopening from its holiday despite August retail sales up 5.6% YoY. Japan traded lower after Tokyo CPI accelerated well above forecast on special factors and higher accommodation charges. Korea edged higher as headline CPI eased to 2.9% YoY from 3.1%. China remains closed for Golden Week.
European equities are higher in a quiet macro session. Front-month Brent is down more than $2 overnight to around $100/bbl, while the US 10-year Treasury yield is unchanged at 5.23%.

GS AI Adoption Tracker (Dong): firm adoption rose 1.4pp in September to an estimated 23.8% among establishments. Labor effects remain visible but narrow, with drags in marketing, graphic design, customer service and some tech roles, offset by data-center construction jobs (+317k since 2022). AI-attributed layoffs were 3.4k in August (203k cumulative since May 2023).

GS sees large productivity gains where AI is deployed but only modest gains economy-wide. Higher-adoption industries now show a slight productivity acceleration in official data. Semiconductor revenue is seen at $868bn by end-2026 and AI-related hardware investment is trending $555bn above its 2022 level (1.7% of GDP).
September payrolls and August factory orders are due today. GS expects nonfarm payrolls of +80k versus consensus +90k and a prior +162k, with the unemployment rate at 4.1% in line with consensus.

Nike (NKE, Neutral, Roach): stock is down 10% pre-market after F1Q27 results. Healthy growth in the performance business is more than offset by pressure in Sportswear, Jordan and China, down LDD%, mid-teens% and 26% ex-FX respectively. FY27 guidance was introduced. The 12m target was cut to $30 from $38 and the November 17 Investor Day is the next catalyst.

Adobe (ADBE, Sell, Borges): the CEO changes on December 1 as part of a planned leadership change. GS notes such changes in software have historically catalyzed strategic change, but ADBE must still prove it can turn its core creative IP into durable AI-led growth amid intensifying competition. 12m target $200.

Medicare Advantage (Fidel): the 2027 landscape supports GS's view that the sector is in year two of margin recovery. Pricing remains disciplined, and GS estimates a 10.5% industry average increase in out-of-pocket limits, which helps medical loss ratios. UNH is rated Buy.

Cigna (CI, Buy, Fidel): after its Investor Day, GS reaffirms the durability of the 10-14% EPS growth target and an updated bridge framework supporting a 2030 adjusted EPS floor of at least $45. Specialty & Care is the core growth engine, alongside a new $3bn modernization and productivity plan. 12m target $352.

Capital markets (Blostein): higher rates are weighing on activity and terminal values, leaving Alts, Wealth Brokers and Exchanges at a 20-30% P/E discount to history. GS sees exchanges as most mispriced versus fundamentals, citing solid 3Q volumes, easier comps into 4Q and underappreciated longer-term tokenization upside.

GS is also constructive on alternatives, where the equity drawdown looks larger than the likely earnings risk. Traditional managers and trust banks are seen as steadier. Top ideas into 3Q: TPG, STEP, APO (Alts), BLK and BEN (traditional managers), TW and ICE (exchanges), BNY and STT (trusts), LPLA (wealth).

Cboe (CBOE) upgraded to Neutral from Sell. GS says risks from new retail-oriented wrappers, the durability of zero-dated index options and the extension of the SPX contract within S&P Global have diminished, and the near-term volume backdrop is supportive. 12m target $300.

Consumer credit (Tong): August trends improved, with y/y declines in delinquencies across non-mortgage categories, though lower-tier performance is mixed. 60+ day delinquencies were 2.71% for bankcards, 3.17% for personal loans and 1.32% for auto. Card originations rose 8.1% and personal loans 9.9%.

FICO (Buy, Tong): FHFA approved a mortgage direct licensing program, expanding distribution and pricing flexibility. FHFA also moved to a single LLPA grid for FICO Classic and VantageScore 4.0, which raises near-term share risk for FICO Classic. GS expects switching frictions and secondary-market reliance to keep any erosion gradual. 12m target $1,322.

Rating changes today: CBOE to Neutral from Sell, MonotaRO (3064.T) to Buy from Neutral on better customer retention, Meitu (1357.HK) to Neutral from Buy on fair valuation, SalMar (SALM.OL) initiated Buy and Mowi (MOWI.OL) initiated Neutral.

Pharma (Richter/Haider): after a China biopharma trip, GS sees a focus on me-too/me-better assets and re-engineering of known targets, with progress toward novel drugs supported by a 5-year plan targeting 25% global share of first-in-class drugs. Obesity and oncology ambitions are accelerating.

Other notable research: Hatzius says Fed Vice Chair Jefferson's remarks hint at an October pause. Oil tail-scenario cross-asset opportunities and exposure to a possible ban on US diesel exports are covered in separate notes. Airlines 3Q preview is marking to market for significantly higher fuel. J&J 3Q26 preview focuses on new product cycles. September US auto SAAR was in the 16.0 mn range. Lithium 2027 supply growth is seen exposed to risk.
